title: Hongdae, Yeonnam & Mangwon (Mapo-gu, Seoul): K-Pop Idol Hangouts & K-Drama Filming Spots Guide
subtitle: BLACKPINK and BTS hangouts, Our Beloved Summer cafes, and the Gyeongui Line Forest Park from Her Private Life, mapped with exact Korean addresses and subway exits.
summary: Mapo-gu holds more than 1,000 records in Korea's public KCISA filming dataset, second only to Jongno. This guide strings together Hongdae, Yeonnam-dong, Mangwon, and Sangam into one walkable K-Pop and K-Drama day, with Korean taxi addresses, subway exits, and local food stops.

sections.heading: Why Mapo-gu Is Seoul's K-Pop and Youth Drama Neighborhood
paragraphs: If Jongno is where Korean dramas go for palaces and hanok, Mapo-gu is where they go for youth. In the public filming-location dataset published by the Korea Culture Information Service Agency (KCISA), Mapo-gu has 1,025 records, the second-highest count of any district in Korea after Jongno-gu. The mix is telling: roughly 400 of those records are streets and public spaces, about 400 are restaurants, and another 160 are cafes. In other words, this is a neighborhood where people eat, drink coffee, and wander, and that is exactly what the cameras capture.

The district stretches from the student streets around Hongik University (Hongdae) and the indie cafes of Yeonnam-dong and Sangsu, down to the Han River at Mangwon, and west to the broadcasting towers of Sangam Digital Media City, where MBC, SBS and other networks have offices. That geography explains the mix of entries: idol vlog cafes in Hongdae, romance-drama dates in Yeonnam, and broadcast-variety restaurant shoots around Sangam.

Among music and idol entries, BLACKPINK (18 records) and BTS (7 records) lead the dataset here, alongside WINNER and OH MY GIRL. On the drama side, the most frequent titles include Because This Is My First Life, My Roommate Is a Gumiho, Nevertheless, What's Wrong with Secretary Kim, Lovestruck in the City, Her Private Life, and Something in the Rain. Food variety shows such as Wednesday Food Talk and Delicious Guys account for many of the restaurant records, which makes Mapo an easy place to eat well while location hunting.

sections.heading: Hongdae and Sangsu: BTS and BLACKPINK Spots
paragraphs: The dataset lists the mural alley at 독막로19길 42 as a jacket-photo location for BTS's LOVE YOURSELF era. The surrounding lanes between Sangsu Station and Hongdae's main streets are packed with graffiti walls that change over time, so the exact mural may look different when you visit. Go before 11 AM for clean shots without crowds.

BLACKPINK has more Mapo-gu entries than any other act. Entries include Insol Coffee in Sangsu (인솔커피 상수점, 독막로18길 16), recorded as the cafe Rosé visited with her dog Hank, and Mon Cafe Gregory (양화로6길 84), which the dataset notes Jisoo praised on Instagram. These are working businesses, so buy a drink, keep photos quick, and check Naver Map for current hours before you go.

The eyewear flagship at 독막로7길 54 appears in Something in the Rain, where Yoon Jin-ah (Son Ye-jin) comes here with coworkers during a lunch break in Episode 12. The store's rotating art installations make it worth a stop even if you are not shopping.

sections.heading: Yeonnam-dong and the Gyeongui Line Forest Park: Romance Drama Walk
paragraphs: Yeonnam-dong is the most relaxed part of this route. A disused railway line was turned into the Gyeongui Line Forest Park, a long, narrow strip of lawn and trees that locals nicknamed "Yeontral Park." According to the dataset, Ryan Gold (Kim Jae-wook) and Sung Duk-mi (Park Min-young) come to a corner of this park on a date in the final episode of Her Private Life (연남로 80).

Two cafes from Our Beloved Summer sit within a short walk of each other on the north side of Yeonnam. Cafe Scone (성미산로 172, 2nd floor) is where Kim Ji-woong (Kim Sung-cheol) tries to persuade Kook Yeon-su (Kim Da-mi) to appear in his documentary, and Mirabeau Patisserie (성미산로29길 35-6) is where Yeon-su's blind date falls apart. The same lanes also appear in More Than Friends, when Kyung Woo-yeon (Shin Ye-eun) and Lee Soo (Ong Seong-wu) explore Yeonnam on foot along 동교로46길.

Just south of Hongik University Station, the book-themed stretch of the old rail line at 와우산로37길 35 is listed as a main backdrop for Welcome to Waikiki. It is free, quiet in the morning, and lined with small bookshops and benches.

In Seogyo-dong, the former residence of President Choi Kyu-hah (동교로15길 10) is recorded as the exterior used for Dong-ryong's house in Reply 1988. It is a heritage house rather than a set, so check opening days on Naver Map before you go.

sections.heading: Mangwon and Sangam: Han River, Sky Park and Broadcast Town
paragraphs: Mangwon Hangang Park (마포나루길 467) appears in Ex-Girlfriend Club, where the area near Seongsan Bridge is a regular meeting spot for the leads. Grab snacks at Mangwon Market first, then walk about 15 minutes to the river for a picnic or a rented bike.

Haneul Park (하늘공원로 95) sits on a former landfill turned into a hilltop grassland. In Go Back Couple Episode 4, Min Seo-young (Go Bo-gyeol) and Choi Ban-do (Son Ho-jun) come here on a date. In October and November the silver grass (eulalia) turns gold, which makes this one of the best autumn photo spots in Seoul. The adjoining World Cup Park (하늘공원로 86) is where the siblings talk things through in Episode 12 of My Unfamiliar Family, and the Peace Park (월드컵로 243-60) is listed as a park RM posted on Twitter.

Five former oil storage tanks were converted into the Oil Tank Culture Park (문화비축기지, 증산로 87). Park Jae-won (Ji Chang-wook) comes here to take photos in Episode 3 of Lovestruck in the City. The concrete-and-steel tanks make a striking contrast with the leafy parks next door.

sections.heading: Where to Eat: Drama Restaurants and Local Favorites
paragraphs: Mapo's restaurant entries lean toward Korean barbecue and casual drinking spots, which is a good match for the dramas they appear in. Mapo Sogeumgui (마포소금구이, 와우산로32길 32) is listed as the pub that Park Sae-ro-yi and his father prepare in Itaewon Class. Seoul Dwaeji-gui (서울돼지구이, 와우산로 15-3) is where Jeon Yeo-been and Son Suk-ku drink soju over grilled pork in Be Melodramatic.

For something lighter, Mangwon Market is famous among locals for cheap street snacks such as fried chicken pieces, croquettes, and hotteok. Yeonnam-dong's side streets are packed with small brunch cafes and bakeries. Because these records come from a public dataset compiled over several years, some businesses may have moved or closed, so always confirm on Naver Map or KakaoMap before making a special trip.

sections.heading: Getting Around Mapo-gu: Subway, Taxi and a Half-Day Route
paragraphs: Hongik University Station (Line 2, AREX Airport Railroad, and Gyeongui-Jungang Line) is the main hub and has a direct train from Incheon Airport. Sangsu and Hapjeong (Line 6, Hapjeong also on Line 2) are best for the mural streets and Sangsu cafes, Mangwon (Line 6) for the market and river, and World Cup Stadium (Line 6) for Haneul Park and the Oil Tank Culture Park.

Copy the Korean addresses in this guide into Kakao T or show them to the driver. Korean road addresses are far more reliable than English place names, and Google Maps walking directions are limited in Korea, so use Naver Map or KakaoMap for navigation.

Start at 10 AM at Hongik University Station Exit 3 and walk the Gyeongui Line Forest Park north into Yeonnam-dong for the Our Beloved Summer cafes. Around noon, head south through Hongdae to the mural streets and Gentle Monster, then have lunch near Sangsu. Take Line 6 three stops to Mangwon for the market and the river, or continue two more stops to World Cup Stadium for a late-afternoon walk up Haneul Park, timed for sunset in autumn.

title: Jongno & Bukchon, Seoul: Complete K-Drama Palace & Hanok Filming Guide (Goblin, Lovely Runner, Queen of Tears)
subtitle: Walk through 600 years of Joseon royal architecture and atmospheric stone-wall alleys featured in Goblin, Kingdom, Lovely Runner, and Mr. Sunshine.
summary: Discover how to explore Seoul's historic heart like a K-Drama location scout—from Deoksugung Stone Wall Road and Bukchon Hanok Village to Anguk's hidden courtyard cafes, subway exits, and Hanbok photo tips.

sections.heading: Why Jongno & Bukchon Are the Beating Heart of K-Drama Cinematography
paragraphs: No district in South Korea appears on global streaming screens more frequently than Jongno-gu and neighboring Jung-gu in central Seoul. Verified records from the Korea Cultural Information Service Agency (KCISA) public filming dataset show hundreds of drama, film, and music video productions clustering around Gyeongbokgung Palace, Changdeokgung Palace, Bukchon Hanok Village, Seochon, and Deoksugung Stone Wall Road.

For international travelers, what makes Jongno extraordinary is its walkable density. Within a single two-kilometer radius, you can stand on the ginkgo-lined stone path where Kim Shin first passed Ji Eun-tak under a rain umbrella in Goblin (Guardian: The Lonely and Great God), climb the curved traditional tiled-roof ridge of Bukchon Hanok Village overlooking modern Seoul towers, and step into the nostalgic neighborhood alleys of Seochon and Ikseon-dong.

sections.heading: Key Verified Filming Locations in This District (With Exact Korean Addresses)
paragraphs: 1. Deoksugung Stone Wall Road (덕수궁 돌담길 — 99 Sejong-daero, Jung-gu, Seoul): Running along the outer wall of Deoksugung Palace from City Hall Station (Subway Line 1 & 2, Exit 1 or 2), this 900-meter pedestrian lane is legendary in Goblin, Do You Like Brahms?, and Lovely Runner. Visit between 8:00 AM and 9:30 AM for soft morning light filtering through the trees, or during late October and November when golden ginkgo leaves carpet the cobblestones.

2. Bukchon Hanok Village Photo Point #6 (북촌한옥마을 — 37 Gyedong-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul): Reached via Anguk Station (Line 3, Exit 2), this uphill residential lane preserves authentic Joseon-era aristocratic homes (hanok). Stand at the top of the slope looking south to capture dark curved clay roofs framing Namsan Seoul Tower in the distance. Remember that Bukchon is an active residential neighborhood with designated visitor hours (10:00 AM–5:00 PM) and quiet-zone etiquette.

3. Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hyangwonjeong Pavilion (경복궁 — 161 Sajik-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul): Accessed directly from Gyeongbokgung Station (Line 3, Exit 5), the royal throne hall (Geunjeongjeon) and water pavilions have anchored Kingdom, The Red Sleeve, Under the Queen's Umbrella, and BTS's iconic 'IDOL' & 'Mikrokosmos' performances on The Tonight Show.

sections.heading: Half-Day Walking Itinerary & Subway Navigation Strategy
paragraphs: Start at Gyeongbokgung Station (Exit 4) at 9:00 AM when palace gates open. Wearing a rented traditional Hanbok grants you free admission to all major royal palaces in Seoul. Spend 90 minutes photographing Geunjeongjeon Hall and Gyeonghoeru Pavilion before exiting via the east gate toward Bukchon Hanok Village.

From Bukchon, stroll downhill into Ikseon-dong Hanok Alley (익선동 한옥거리) for lunch—where early-1920s courtyard houses have been transformed into sunlit soufflé pancake cafes, salt-bread bakeries, and craft tea houses featured in Hotel Del Luna and Queen of Tears. Finish your afternoon with a 15-minute walk along Cheonggyecheon Stream to Deoksugung Stone Wall Road at golden hour.

sections.heading: Where to Eat, Stay & Book Local Passes in Jongno
paragraphs: Local Culinary Highlights: Don't miss Tosokchon Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup inside a grand hanok near Gyeongbokgung), Hwangsaengga Kalguksu (Michelin Bib Gourmand hand-cut noodle soup and giant steamed dumplings in Bukchon), and Onion Anguk for pastries under a traditional wooden roof.

Where to Stay: Choosing a hotel in Insadong, Myeongdong, or Gwanghwamun puts you within walking distance of all four royal palaces and direct Airport Railroad / Limousine Bus connections to Incheon International Airport (ICN).

title: Suwon Hwaseong & Haenggung-dong: Why Korea's UNESCO Fortress City Is the #1 K-Drama Filming Neighborhood
subtitle: From Sol and Sun-jae's iconic blue-and-yellow gate houses in Lovely Runner to Our Beloved Summer and Extraordinary Attorney Woo.
summary: Just 35 minutes south of Seoul Station by KTX or Subway Line 1, Suwon's Haenggung-dong mural alleys and UNESCO Hwaseong Fortress walls host Korea's highest concentration of youth romance K-Drama scenes.

sections.heading: How Haenggung-dong Became Korea's Capital of Youth & Romance K-Dramas
paragraphs: If you have watched Lovely Runner (선재 업고 튀어), Our Beloved Summer (그해 우리는), Extraordinary Attorney Woo (이상한 변호사 우영우), or Itaewon Class, you have already fallen in love with Haenggung-dong in Suwon. Located directly inside the 5.7-kilometer stone ramparts of the UNESCO World Heritage Hwaseong Fortress, this low-rise neighborhood bans high-rise apartment towers to preserve historic sightlines.

Because the streets retain warm brick houses, flowering wall vines, stone bridges over the Suwoncheon Stream, and panoramic sunset fortress gates, Korean television directors repeatedly choose Haenggung-dong to portray nostalgic high school and university neighborhoods.

sections.heading: Must-Visit Verified Filming Spots in Suwon (Step-by-Step Route)
paragraphs: 1. Im Sol & Ryu Sun-jae's Houses (화성행궁 행리단길 몽테드 — 14 Hwaseomun-ro 48beon-gil, Paldal-gu, Suwon): The viral yellowumbrella corner where Im Sol runs out to meet Ryu Sun-jae in Lovely Runner sits right in the heart of Haengnidan-gil. The two houses face each other across a charming narrow lane, just a 4-minute walk from Hwaseomun Gate.

2. Choi Ung's House & Jangangiun Fortress Wall Path (장안공원 성곽길 — 293 Jeongjo-ro, Paldal-gu, Suwon): Just north of Hwaseomun Gate, the curving stone fortress wall and rooftop terrace served as illustrator Choi Ung's home in Our Beloved Summer. Walking the outer fortress trail during sunset gives you golden light across both ancient battlements and neighborhood rooftops.

3. Woo Young-woo Gimbap Shop (우영우 김밥집 / 카자구루마 — 61 Sinpung-ro 23beon-gil, Paldal-gu, Suwon): Situated along the same walkable Haengnidan-gil cafe street, the exterior of Young-woo's father's gimbap diner is an active Japanese fusion restaurant where fans stop for photos.

sections.heading: How to Get to Suwon from Seoul & Local Food Specialties
paragraphs: Fastest Transit from Seoul: Board a KTX, ITX-Saemaeul, or Mugunghwa train from Seoul Station or Yongsan Station to Suwon Station (25–32 minutes), or take Seoul Subway Line 1 / Bundang Line directly to Suwon Station. From Suwon Station Exit 4, hop on local bus #11, #13, or a 10-minute taxi ride straight to Hwaseong Haenggung Temporary Palace (화성행궁).

Suwon's Famous Dish — Suwon Wang-Galbi (Marinated Beef Short Ribs): Since the 1940s, Suwon has been famous across Korea for giant charcoal-grilled beef short ribs seasoned with sesame oil, garlic, and Korean pear, alongside Suwon 통닭거리 (Suwon Fried Chicken Street) right by Paldalmun Gate where Extreme Job was inspired.

title: Gangneung & Jumunjin East Coast Guide: From the Iconic Goblin Breakwater to BTS Bus Stop & Anmok Coffee Street
subtitle: Plan the ultimate 1-day KTX East Sea pilgrimage across Gangwon Province's turquoise beaches, buckwheat fields, and oceanfront roasteries.
summary: Only 1 hour and 50 minutes from Seoul Station on the KTX-Eum high-speed train, Gangneung's Jumunjin coastline combines the Goblin red-scarf breakwater and BTS's 'You Never Walk Alone' album cover bus stop.

sections.heading: Why Gangneung Is Korea's #1 Coastal Pilgrimage for K-Drama & K-Pop Fans
paragraphs: Stretching along the crystal-clear East Sea in Gangwon Province, Gangneung (강릉) offers a dramatic coastal contrast to Seoul's neon skyline. Thanks to the KTX Gangneung Line built for the 2018 Winter Olympics, travelers can board a high-speed train at Seoul Station or Cheongnyangni Station in the morning and stand beside crashing turquoise waves under two hours later.

Two of the most photographed pop-culture landmarks in modern Korean history sit just 3.5 kilometers apart along the northern Jumunjin shoreline: the stone breakwater where Ji Eun-tak first summoned Kim Shin by blowing out a birthday candle in Goblin (Guardian), and the pastel oceanfront bus stop reproduced for BTS's 'You Never Walk Alone' ('Spring Day') album jacket.

sections.heading: Exact Coordinates & Photography Tips Along Jumunjin Coast
paragraphs: 1. Jumunjin Breakwater — Goblin Red Scarf Pier (주문진 방사제 — 1609 Haean-ro, Jumunjin-eup, Gangneung-si): Unlike the northern fishery harbor breakwater, the exact filming jetty is opposite café street at Yeongjin Beach / Jumunjin southern coastal road. Nearby cafés rent red knit scarves and white buckwheat flower bouquets so you can recreate the exact framing from Episode 1.

2. BTS Bus Stop at Hyangho Beach (주문진 BTS 버스정류장 — 210-125 Hyangho-ri, Jumunjin-eup, Gangneung-si): Built at the exact spot on the sandy edge of Hyangho Beach where BTS photographed the 'You Never Walk Alone' jacket, this shelter looks directly out over the horizon of the East Sea. Arrive before 10:00 AM on weekdays for clear, queue-free photos.

3. Anmok Beach Coffee Street (안목해변 커피거리 — Changhae-ro 14beon-gil, Gangneung-si): After exploring Jumunjin in the morning, head south to Anmok Beach, where over 30 specialty coffee roasteries line the white-sand promenade with multi-story glass windows overlooking the waves.

sections.heading: Local Gangneung Delicacies & KTX Travel Tips
paragraphs: Must-Eat Dishes in Gangneung: Chodang Sundubu (초당순두부 — silky uncurdled tofu simmered with clean East Sea seawater, including spicy seafood jjamppong sundubu and black-sesame sundubu gelato), Jumunjin fresh snow crab & raw fish market, and Gangneung Jungang Market's crispy dakgangjeong (sweet-spicy glazed chicken).

Transportation Tip: Book your round-trip KTX tickets to Gangneung Station at least 1–2 weeks in advance if traveling on a Friday or weekend. From Gangneung KTX Station, Gangneung City sets up an official Tourist Taxi program (3-hour flat-rate private taxi) that covers Jumunjin Breakwater, BTS Bus Stop, Arte Museum, and Anmok Beach seamlessly.

title: Itaewon, Namsan & Yongsan: Walking Through Itaewon Class, HYBE K-Pop Landmarks & Seoul Skyline Filming Spots
subtitle: Follow Park Sae-royi's footsteps from Noksapyeong Overpass and Danbam rooftops up to Namsan Seoul Tower and Yongsan's K-Pop hub.
summary: Yongsan-gu connects Seoul's most famous panoramic observatory—Namsan Seoul Tower—with the hillside rooftop bars of Haebangchon, Itaewon Class pedestrian bridges, and the global headquarters of HYBE.

sections.heading: Why Yongsan & Namsan Deliver the Ultimate Seoul Panorama
paragraphs: Rising 243 meters at the geographical center of Seoul, Namsan Mountain and the surrounding neighborhoods of Yongsan-gu (Itaewon, Haebangchon, Gyeongnidan, and Hangangjin) create dramatic multi-level streetscapes. Steep hillside stairs, pedestrian overpasses framing Namsan Seoul Tower, and rooftop terraces overlooking the Han River make Yongsan a visual signature of modern K-Dramas.

In Itaewon Class, almost every pivotal turning point in Park Sae-royi's journey was filmed along the ridge connecting Noksapyeong Station, Haebangchon (HBC), and Huam-dong's Namsan Park Fortress Wall trail.

sections.heading: Top Verified Filming Spots in Yongsan-gu
paragraphs: 1. Noksapyeong Pedestrian Overpass (녹사평역 육교 — 195 Noksapyeong-daero, Yongsan-gu, Seoul): Step out of Noksapyeong Station (Subway Line 6, Exit 3) and walk 150 meters onto the steel pedestrian bridge. Looking north, the avenue curves uphill directly toward Namsan Seoul Tower—the exact frame where Park Sae-royi stands deep in thought throughout Itaewon Class.

2. Oriole & The Finest Rooftop Line in Haebangchon (해방촌 루프탑 거리 — Sinheung-ro, Yongsan-gu, Seoul): Climb the hillside road toward Namsan Sowol-gil to find the real-life rooftop pub buildings featured as the second Danbam location and finale kiss viewpoint.

3. Namsan Seoul Tower & Locks of Love Terrace (남산서울타워 — 105 Namsangongwon-gil, Yongsan-gu, Seoul): Featured in Boys Over Flowers, My Love from the Star, True Beauty, and Legend of the Blue Sea, the Namsan Cable Car and Namsan Observation Deck remain Seoul's #1 romantic landmark.

sections.heading: Combining Namsan with HYBE Insight Cafe District in Yongsan
paragraphs: Ten minutes southwest of Noksapyeong by subway or bus lies Hangang-daero near Sinyongsan Station (Line 4, Exit 2), home to the HYBE Headquarters building. The blocks behind HYBE are packed with fan-favorite specialty coffee shops, birthday event cafes, and traditional Korean barbecue restaurants frequented by K-Pop artists and choreographers.

Best Time to Visit: Start at Sinyongsan / HYBE in the early afternoon, ride Line 6 to Noksapyeong Overpass & Haebangchon around 4:30 PM for golden hour, and take the Namsan Circular Bus (#01A or #01B) up to Namsan Seoul Tower just as the city lights switch on.
